html:
SMTO-LLM-0056 — The AI model didn't use the action this step required

GUID: 55db06a4-1834-4edf-9148-c7199e8de9f5
Slug: model-tool-choice-invalid
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • For this step, SMTO needed the model to use one specific action. The model answered with something else, such as plain text or a different action, so SMTO stopped the step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the steps already shown for this task in the conversation and note which ones finished before the error. Work finished before this reply still stands, so you only need SMTO to continue, not redo it.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and pick a different model for Main (and Helper, if one is set), then save. Some models ignore a request to use one particular action; another model usually follows it.
  3. If someone else runs your AI model server, ask them to make sure it supports choosing a specific tool, not only free answers. Without that support, the server can let the model answer in text when an action was required.
  4. Send a new message asking SMTO to continue from where it stopped, without repeating the steps that already finished. With a model that follows the request, this step can finish and the task moves on.

What success looks like

  • The step that stopped completes, and the task moves on to its next step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; if the details mention no tools being offered, it's a problem in SMTO itself. Don't turn off any of SMTO's safety checks to get past it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The tool choice for this bounded turn and the response disagree: a named or required tool choice had no tools advertised, tool_choice 'none' would remove the turn's required tool access, the model called a different function than the one required, or it returned text where only the named tool call is allowed.

What this means

  • The requested or returned tool choice conflicts with the bounded call contract, including missing advertised tools, forbidden text or removal of required tool access. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The requested or returned tool choice conflicts with the bounded call contract, including missing advertised tools, forbidden text or removal of required tool access.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the advertised tools, requested tool choice and whether this internal turn permits prose; missing tools and unexpected accompanying text require different repairs.

How to fix it

  • Compare the advertised tools, requested tool_choice and the returned message in Technical details. If the endpoint ignores named or required tool_choice, enable tool-choice support (vLLM: --enable-auto-tool-choice with the correct --tool-call-parser) or route to a model that honours it; a named choice with no tools advertised, or tool_choice 'none', is an SMTO defect to report with the error ID. Keep the validator in place.
  • Restore agreement between the advertised tools, requested choice and permitted response content. Keep the bounded validator in place; report a persistent mismatch with the occurrence ID.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The requested choice and returned envelope both satisfy the same advertised bounded contract.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
